title: The diagonal lemma for the first-order calculus (OPEN; the arithmetization half and the Leibniz rule are landed, representability in Q is not)
statement: For every formula psi with one free variable there is a sentence delta such that the theory proves delta if and only if it proves psi applied to the numeral of delta's own Goedel number. STILL NOT ESTABLISHED HERE, but both prerequisites this row recorded are now discharged and the remaining obstruction is a different one. (i) The diagonalization function is built and its identity is PROVED: FO.Code.diagAux sends the code of p to the code of p with the numeral of its own code substituted, and FO.Code.diagAux_code says so (F:fo-diagonal-identity), on top of the decoder round trip and the commuting lemma. (ii) The calculus HAS a Leibniz rule as of ADR-1648: FO.Provable.eqf_subst, the seventeenth constructor, with its soundness case, so a proof that substitutes one numeral for another under a formula IS expressible. What remains is neither of those: the biconditional needs Gamma_Q to PROVE the numeric fact diag m-bar = code delta, i.e. the diagonal function must be REPRESENTABLE in Q, which for a Nat.rec-defined function is Sigma-1 completeness. Nothing in fo_*.rs relates FO.Provable to a computation on Nat in either direction; FO.Formula has no Iff connective (it would be and_ (imp a b) (imp b a)); and representing diag means representing FO.Code.pair, FO.Code.tri, FO.Code.unpair and the fuel recursion. That is a strand, not a step.

formal.statement: theorem FO.diagonal : ((x0 : FO.Context) -> ((x1 : FO.Formula) -> Exists.{1} FO.Formula (fun (x2 : FO.Formula) => Iff (FO.Provable x0 x2) (FO.Provable x0 (FO.Formula.subst x1 (FO.Subst.cons (FO.Formula.numeral (FO.Formula.code x2)) FO.Subst.id))))))

provenance.source: this row records the measured remaining gap after lane arithmetization landed the numbering and its injectivity (W3-7, ADR-1640)

prior_art.what: the fixed-point construction; Carnap gave the general diagonal lemma Goedel used in the special case
prior_art.attribution: standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary sources

notes:
THE STATEMENT IS AUTHORED, NOT EXTRACTED. Neither FO.diagonal nor FO.Formula.numeral exists in the kernel, so the binder indices and the shape above are this lane's, not Kernel::render_lean's. It is written in the style render_lean produces. FO.Formula.numeral is the missing 'closed term denoting a given natural' -- with the signature fo_syntax.rs gives (FO.Term.f0 for constants, FO.Term.f1 for unary function symbols) it is the iterated successor term, one f1 per unit, so it is a Nat.rec and is NOT the hard part.

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM F:fo-formula-decoder. The two obstructions are different in kind and a later lane needs to know which it is walking into.

(1) THE BINDING ONE IS THE DECODER, and it is ordinary construction work sized in F:fo-formula-decoder: a fuel-recursive decodeAux, a fuel-agreement lemma, and a depth-versus-code bound. Until it exists the diagonalization function cannot be written down, so the statement above cannot even be REACHED as a goal.

(2) THE SECOND IS A MISSING RULE, and it is a design decision rather than a gap. ADR-1636 records that FO.Provable's only equality rule is eqf_refl, and that the Leibniz rule -- from s = t and phi[s] infer phi[t] -- is sound but not landed, because its soundness case needs a congruence of FO.sat along an equality between the evaluations of two terms under a substitution, i.e. a fifth induction over FO.Formula that slice did not build. The diagonal lemma's biconditional needs exactly that rule. Landing it is one induction plus one soundness minor, and it must keep FO.soundness green.

WHICH FRAGMENT. The classical statement is over a theory containing Robinson arithmetic Q, not over PA: what the argument uses is that the theory proves the numeral facts about successor, addition and multiplication and the ordering, not induction. In this ledger that would be a specific FO.Context of Q's axioms written in the fo_syntax.rs signature, and no such context exists yet; naming it is part of the same increment as (2).

UPDATE 2026-09-05 (lane fo-diagonal, ADR-1648). This row's two recorded prerequisites are discharged. The first -- 'defining d means decoding, which is the open fact F:fo-formula-decoder' -- is met at EXPLICIT fuel rather than by the self-fuelled decoder: the self-fuelled wrapper turned out to need Nat.le (size p) (code p), which is FALSE, so FO.Code.diagAux takes its fuel as an argument and F:fo-diagonal-identity is stated there. The second -- 'no Leibniz rule' -- is met outright by FO.Provable.eqf_subst.

A MEASURED HAZARD FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS NEXT. The diagonal is not EVALUABLE in this kernel at any genuine code. Numerals are unary, and diagAux (code p) contains FO.Term.code (FO.Term.numeral (FO.Formula.code p)); at FO.Formula.eqf (var 0) (var 0) (code 2) the diagonalised code is over ten million, and at FO.Formula.rel1 0 (var 0) (code 5) it overflows the stack. Any test of a diagonal construction has to be symbolic. This is also why 'just compute delta and check it' is not an available shortcut to the biconditional.

THE FORMAL STATEMENT ABOVE STILL NAMES FO.Formula.numeral, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST. The numeral landed as FO.Term.numeral : Nat -> FO.Term, which is the right type -- a numeral is a term, and FO.Formula.subst takes a substitution into terms. Whoever proves this row should restate it against FO.Term.numeral rather than inherit the authored name.
